newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower, perch above 3,200 support.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower, perch above 3,200 support.

text.p: * Absence of foreign funds limits turnover at 1.9 bln pesos
The Manila share index resumed its downtrend on Friday as foreign funds remained sidelined due to the absence of fresh trading impetus, brokers said.
"The market traded relatively flat throughout the session, with some pockets of strength," Poch Zamora, head of dealing at Peregrine Securities, said.
The key index shed 5.02 points, or 0.16 percent, to close at 3,201.65 after trading under the 3,200 level for most of the day.
Value turnover was limited to 1.9 billion pesos as most investors opted to stay out of the market.
Manila shares have been in a slump since the start of the month due to a dearth of trading factors. The index snapped a seven-day losing streak on Thursday due to technical buying.

The decline in the index on Friday was capped as local players picked up media giant ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp, which gained 50 centavos to 32 pesos, and holding firm Filinvest Development Corp, which rose 10 centavos to 7.40 pesos.
"It seems that there is strong support at 3,200," Bing Trinidad, head of marketing at DBS Securities, said.
Other blue chips maintained their previous day's closing prices due to lack of interest.
Brokers said they expected the market to drift cautiously sideways next week due to the four-day Easter weekend as well as the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting earlier in the week.
Trinidad said select mining shares such as Lepanto Consolidated and United Paragon Mining, which were two of the actively traded issues on Friday, will continue to hog punters' attention.
